transcript.content: Hello, welcome. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi… thank you. I guess what finally made me come in is, um, I’ve been feeling kind of… flattened, maybe? Not in a dramatic way. I’m still doing what I need to do, mostly. But the part of me that used to reach out to people, and enjoy my work, or yoga, or going to galleries, even journaling… it’s gotten very quiet.

I don’t know if that’s the right way to put it. I just feel like I’m moving through obligations more than really being in my life.
Have you noticed a loss of interest or pleasure in activities that you used to enjoy, like yoga, going to galleries, or journaling?

Yes… I think so. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is—I’m still getting through things, and I do what I’m supposed to do—but the wanting part is just… quieter.

Like with yoga or galleries, or even journaling, I used to feel drawn to them. Now it’s more like I remember that I used to like them, but I don’t really reach for them. Same with work and people, honestly. I’m mostly just moving through obligations. Does that make sense?
Have you noticed feeling down or depressed most of the day, even if it's not severe?

I’m not sure I’d call it depressed, exactly. I mean, I have low moments, but not like I’m crying all day or unable to function. It’s more… muted, maybe. Kind of flat.

Most of the day? I don’t know. I’m still doing what I need to do, so I don’t want to overstate it. But there is this heaviness or dullness that’s there a lot of the time. Does that count as feeling down?
Can you think of a time recently when you felt genuine enjoyment or interest in something? Even small things—like a conversation, a meal, or a moment of quiet?

I can think of little moments where something is… pleasant, I guess. Like a quiet cup of coffee, or a nice exchange with someone. So it’s not that I feel nothing.

But genuine enjoyment, like really being pulled toward something? That’s harder. The part of me that used to reach for people, or feel interested in work, or want to go to yoga or a gallery, or even sit down and journal… it’s just gotten very quiet. I mostly do what I’m supposed to do, and I’m grateful I can, but it feels more like moving through obligations than really enjoying them. Does that answer what you mean?
How long have you been feeling this way? Has this sense of flatness or muted interest been going on for most days over the past couple of years, or is it more recent, like within the past few months?

I don’t think it’s been years, no. It feels more recent than that… maybe about eight months or so.

It kind of started after we took my older relative into our apartment. I don’t want to make it sound like I’m blaming that, because we’re managing, and it’s the right thing to do. But since then, this whole change in how I’m thinking, working, and connecting with people has been there most days. The flatness, the muted interest… it’s been around since then, I think. Does that timeframe make sense?
Can you tell me if you’ve noticed a significant loss of interest or pleasure in most activities, even ones you used to enjoy, not just a quieting or muted interest?

Yes… I think so. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, because I’m still showing up and doing things, but the honest answer is yes.

The part of me that used to really reach for people, or feel satisfied by my work, or want to go to yoga, see a gallery, sit and journal… it’s just gone very quiet. I still do some of those things, or I think about doing them, but it feels more like I’m moving through obligations than actually taking pleasure in them.

So yes, I guess it is more than just being a little muted. Does that make sense?

Can you confirm if this sense of flatness and loss of interest has been present nearly every day for at least two weeks at a time, and if so, has it been going on without a break for most of the time since it started?

Yes… I think I can confirm that. It’s been there nearly every day, at least in stretches longer than two weeks, and honestly it hasn’t really lifted in any clear way.

It’s been about eight months now, since we took my older relative into our apartment. I don’t mean every single minute is awful or anything—I can still function and have decent moments—but this overall change in how I’m thinking, working, and connecting with people has been there most of the time since then. Is that the kind of timeframe you’re asking about?
Have you noticed any significant changes in your ability to function at work, at home, or in social situations because of this flatness or loss of interest?

Yes… a bit. I mean, I’m still going to work, and I don’t think I’m falling apart or anything. But I’m not functioning at my usual level.

I’ve missed some grant deadlines, which is embarrassing to say. And my supervisor has kind of quietly moved some of my more demanding clients to other clinicians. She’s been kind about it, so I don’t want to overstate it, but I think she’s noticed I’m not as sharp or as engaged as I usually am.

At home and socially, it’s more that I’m doing the minimum. But work is where it’s probably most obvious. Is that the kind of impairment you mean?
In the past two weeks, have you had days where you felt down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day?

I’m not sure I’d call it depressed most of the day, nearly every day… I don’t want to overstate it.

There have been days where I feel low or kind of heavy, but it’s not always clear to me if that’s the same as being depressed in the way you mean. It’s more like I’m muted or worn down. So… I don’t know if I can honestly say yes to “most of the day, nearly every day” in the past two weeks. Does that answer it okay?
Over the past two weeks, have you had several days where you felt down or sad for most of the day, even if it wasn't severe?

Maybe several days, yes… but I’m a little unsure about the “most of the day” part.

I’ve had some days where I felt sad or kind of low, but it hasn’t felt dramatic or constant. More like it comes in the background, if that makes sense. I don’t want to exaggerate it, but I also don’t want to dismiss it if it matters.
In the past two weeks, have you had several days where your mood was clearly down or sad for most of the day, even if it wasn’t severe?

I’m honestly not sure I can say it was clearly down for most of the day. Maybe there were moments, or parts of days, where I felt low, but “clearly sad most of the day” feels stronger than what I’ve noticed.

I don’t want to minimize it if you think it counts, but I also don’t want to say yes just to fit the question.
Over the past two weeks, have you had several days where your mood was low enough that you would clearly say you were depressed, even if it wasn’t severe, for most of the day on those days?

I don’t think I could clearly say I was depressed for most of the day on several days, no. I mean… I’ve had low moments, and maybe I haven’t felt like myself at times, but calling it “depressed” feels like I’d be making it sound stronger than it was.

If that distinction makes sense. I’m trying to answer it accurately.
Over the past eight months, have there been any two-week periods where your mood was clearly down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day, even if it wasn’t severe?

I don’t think so… at least, not that I can clearly identify.

Over eight months, I’ve definitely had rough patches or days where I felt lower, but a full two weeks where it was most of the day, nearly every day—that sounds more definite than what I remember. I’d say I haven’t noticed it in that pattern, unless I’m missing something you’d count differently.
Over the past eight months, have there been times when you felt a clear sense of sadness or depression for most of the day, even if it wasn’t severe, on most days?

I don’t think I’ve had that in a clear, consistent way. I mean, there have been times I felt off or kind of low, but most of the day on most days… I don’t think I could honestly say that.

I’m trying not to underreport it, but I also don’t want to overstate it. From what I’ve noticed, it hasn’t really been a steady sadness or depression like that.
